During this time you can also cause the creature to use a reaction, but this requires you to use your own reaction as well. Each time the target takes damage, it makes a new Cool saving throw against the program. If the saving throw succeeds, the program ends. At Higher Levels. When you execute this program using a 6th-level Execution Slot, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. When you use a 7th-level Execution Slot, the duration is concentration, up to 1 hour. When you use an Execution Slot of 8th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours.

programs.title: Remote Surveillance [Scrying]
programs.requirements: Actual reachable sensor, stored record or communications/analysis system appropriate to the query. Missing evidence gives an explicit gap; no omniscience.
programs.text: Tier 5; 10 minutes; remote network; concentration up to ten minutes. Access an actual existing sensor route observing a chosen creature or familiar location. For a defended creature, Cool save with familiarity modifier: only secondhand+5, met+0, familiar−5; a current authenticated image contributes−2, a personally linked device−4, a valid biometric/session credential−10, using only the strongest credential modifier. Success prevents this program against that target for 24 h. Failure grants actual camera/audio feed, not a hovering omniscient eye. A willing target may fail voluntarily. No sensor means no view, irrespective of name, hair or portrait. Location access uses its real security permissions rather than a fabricated creature save.

programs.title: Secure Network Enclave [Hallow]
programs.requirements: Accessible compatible controllers and a live route for the addressed security/defence process. Can manipulate ongoing network operations; cannot remove permanent hardware, undo finished injury or suppress independent mundane weapons. Wireless upload within printed range is part of execution; use only the printed attack/save, without a preliminary scan or breach check. A printed Touch range remains Touch.
programs.text: Tier 5; 24 hours; touch; until cleared. Configure an actual security domain up to 60-foot radius; overlapping an existing Secure Network Enclave prevents execution; requires installed controllers and consumable configuration supplies. Chosen autonomous synthetic categories cannot open sessions across its boundary without permission. They cannot impose charm/fear/control through the protected domain. On entry, the domain clears such effects imposed by the excluded synthetic categories through that protected interface. Choose one additional mode affecting declared eligible connected recipients: fear suppression; fear induction (Cool save); bodily damage resistance to one of Thermal, Cryogenic, Electrical, Corrosive, Toxic, Concussive or Neural; bodily vulnerability to one of those same seven types (Cool save); powered bright lighting; controlled blackout; isolation from external neural messages; secure local translation; cold-storage preservation of supplied remains; or acoustic isolation that prevents sound leaving or entering the domain. Effects need their actual equipment and do not alter bare biology. An eligible recipient can make a Cool saving throw against the selected extra effect when it enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. Success lets it ignore that extra effect until it leaves the area; failure leaves it eligible to save on later qualifying turns. No resurrection restriction, alignment detector or physical forcefield. Installed equipment and deliberate operating expenses remain real.

programs.title: Sleep Interface [Dream]
programs.requirements: Compatible reachable neural, sensory or motor-control cyberware supporting the specific effect. A motor effect requires motor access; mind/sensory manipulation requires a corresponding neural route. Ordinary unaugmented people cannot be affected directly. Hostile control does not dictate the protagonist’s opinions or voluntary dialogue. Wireless upload within printed range is part of execution; use only the printed attack/save, without a preliminary scan or breach check. A printed Touch range remains Touch.
programs.text: 5th-level illusion Execution: 1 minute Range: Special Duration: 8 hours This program shapes a creature's dreams. Choose a creature known to you as the target of this program. The target must have a compatible sleeping neural interface reachable through an actual route. Creatures that do not sleep cannot be contacted by this Program. You, or a willing creature you touch, enters a trance state, acting as a messenger. While in the trance, the messenger is aware of his or her surroundings, but can't take actions or move. If the target is asleep, the messenger appears in the target's dreams and can converse with the target as long as it remains asleep, through the duration of the program. The messenger can also shape the environment of the dream, creating landscapes, objects, and other images. The messenger can emerge from the trance at any time, ending the effect of the program early. The target recalls the dream perfectly upon waking. If the target is awake when you execute the program, the messenger knows it, and can either end the trance (and the program) or wait for the target to fall asleep, at which point the messenger appears in the target's dreams. You can make the messenger appear monstrous and terrifying to the target. If you do, the messenger can deliver a message of no more than ten words and then the target must make a Cool saving throw. On a failed save, echoes of the phantasmal monstrosity spawn a nightmare that lasts the duration of the target's sleep and prevents the target from gaining any benefit from that rest. In addition, when the target wakes up, it takes 3d6 neural damage. A valid authenticated neural credential grants disadvantage on the target’s save; a body part, photograph or hair grants no network access.

programs.title: Squad Neural Link [Telepathic Bond]
programs.requirements: Actual reachable sensor, stored record or communications/analysis system appropriate to the query. Missing evidence gives an explicit gap; no omniscience.
programs.text: Tier 5; action; 30 feet initial pairing; one hour; ritual. Pair up to eight willing creatures with Intelligence≥3 through actual neural/receiver hardware. Share decoded messages regardless of spoken language through a real routed connection. No thought reading or unlimited reach without infrastructure. An offline/unaugmented recipient needs an actual ordinary receiver for translated audio instead of a neural link.

programs.title: System Lock
programs.requirements: Compatible electronic or neural target as specified; wireless upload within range.
programs.text: Tier 5, enchantment. Lists: Netrunner, Neural Adept, Contractor. One action; 60 feet; concentration, up to one minute. One autonomous synthetic or living human with a neural or motor-control Cyberware makes an INT save. On failure it is restrained and cannot take reactions. It repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the power on success. It retains actions and may attack, use powers or clear the effect through an appropriate countermeasure; this is not paralysis. Upcasting adds one eligible target per tier above 5, all within 30 feet of the first. Each target has its own saves; one casting uses one concentration slot.

programs.title: Vertical Burn [Flame Strike]
programs.requirements: A reachable ignition/heat controller and sufficient actual fuel or rated heating apparatus for the printed area and damage. Fuel is consumed; sustained effects need continuing fuel. A bare battery/spark is not a room-sized explosive source. Portable apparatus must actually be present and capable. The device may belong to anyone. Execution includes overriding its controller; no ownership, pairing or preliminary breach is required. See chapter 02 for environmental control and occupied-device resistance.
programs.text: Tier 5; action; 60 feet; instantaneous. A reachable industrial burner/munitions system with sufficient fuel delivers a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high column at a point in range. Creatures inside make REF saves: 8d6 thermal damage on failure, half on success. Each tier above 5 adds 1d6 thermal. This is one combined thermal damage component. Requires actual fuel, capacity and physical delivery.

programs.title: Combat Chassis Refit [Create Undead]
programs.requirements: Existing reachable combat machines matching the chosen profiles, with actual controllers, weapons and payloads. Each locked standby or hostile active unit makes one Intelligence security save against Program Save DC; unsecured/authorised units require none. Standby must have live electronics; unpowered/isolated units need actual power/access. Chapter02 applies.
programs.text: Tier6; one minute; range10 feet; duration24 hours after installation; no ongoing Concentration. Install coordinated control on up to3 actual Assault Units from chapter09. Tier7:4 Assault Units. Tier8:5 Assault Units, or2 Hazmat Assault Units, or2 Command Units. Tier9:6 Assault Units, or3 Hazmat Assault Units, or3 Command Units, or2 Siege Units. Extended installation spends an Action and Concentration each turn until complete. Bonus Action issues the same routed command to any/all controlled units within120 feet. Queued achievable orders continue through link loss; otherwise defend. Each unit has one normal turn, no autonomous Program execution or recursive creation. Renew before expiry with another execution of sufficient capacity. Expiry ends the routine, leaving ordinary owned functions or restoring established prior controller/failsafe; halt if none. Preserve HP, battery, fuel and ammunition. Actual reset, power loss, counterhack or destruction can stop the daemon. Permanent ownership requires separate credential/security work.

programs.title: Full-Spectrum Diagnostics [True Seeing]
programs.requirements: A willing recipient’s electronic optics and Cyberdeck.
programs.text: Tier 6; Action; Touch; 1 hour. Advanced feed reconstruction and authentication give a willing recipient 120-foot true visual diagnostics: detect optical camouflage, recognise fabricated images and disguises, and see normally despite software-induced darkness. Recover actual visible outlines from available sensor data. Physical opaque barriers and absent light/sensor data remain genuine limits. No consumable diagnostic implant is required.

programs.title: Group Behaviour Injection [Mass Suggestion]
programs.requirements: Compatible reachable neural, sensory or motor-control cyberware supporting the specific effect. A motor effect requires motor access; mind/sensory manipulation requires a corresponding neural route. Ordinary unaugmented people cannot be affected directly. Hostile control does not dictate the protagonist’s opinions or voluntary dialogue. Wireless upload within printed range is part of execution; use only the printed attack/save, without a preliminary scan or breach check. A printed Touch range remains Touch.
programs.text: 6th-level enchantment Execution: 1 action Range: 60 feet Duration: 24 hours You suggest a course of activity (limited to a sentence or two) and influence through the compatible neural interface up to twelve creatures of your choice that you can see within range and that can receive and interpret your transmitted instructions. Creatures that can't be charmed are immune to this effect. The suggestion must be worded in such a manner as to make the course of action sound reasonable. Asking the creature to stab itself, throw itself onto a spear, immolate itself, or do some other obviously harmful act automatically negates the effect of the program. Each target must make a Cool saving throw. On a failed save, it pursues the course of action you described to the best of its ability. The suggested course of action can continue for the entire duration. If the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the program ends when the subject finishes what it was asked to do. You can also specify conditions that will trigger a special activity during the duration. For example, you might suggest that a group of soldiers give all their money to the first beggar they meet. profiles.title: Senda Mobility Sidewinder H4 — Hoverboard / Sensor Scout
profiles.text:
Senda Mobility is an independent Osaka manufacturer of compact commuter boards and courier equipment. Introduced in 2064, the Sidewinder H4 uses a rounded rectangular deck, recessed foot grips, replaceable rubber edge strips and shrouded electric lift fans beneath the board. Stock finishes include graphite, faded cream and red. The carried unit is 115 cm long, 32 cm wide and 11 cm thick, weighing 11 kg.

**Stock board.** Small vehicle; AC 13, HP 15; BOD 6 REF 15 CON 13 INT 3 TECH 3 COOL 10; ordinary saves/checks use these scores. Consumer security+0 if a security save is required. Immune Toxic and Neural damage and Poisoned; no special physical resistances. One rider with up to 120 kg total rider/cargo, within about 30 cm of a firm surface. Loaded hover speed 60 feet; Dash 120 feet. Straight clear-route cruising maximum 30 km/h; combat manoeuvring uses the printed speeds. Uneven ground is difficult terrain; a gap cannot be crossed unless actual momentum/clearance permits a normal adjudicated manoeuvre. It cannot carry an adult upward into free flight. Unloaded it can fly 60 feet using the same fans, or manoeuvre along the surface at 15 feet; free-flight cargo limit 5 kg. It cannot operate submerged.

**Power and control.** Battery capacity 120 operating minutes. Each minute of ordinary surface travel uses 1; continuous Dash/high-speed cruise or unloaded free flight uses 2. Two-hour full recharge from a suitable mains charger; a depleted pack can be physically swapped in one minute. Powered standby uses 1 operating minute per 24 hours. One charge powers sensors and communications alongside locomotion, not separate simultaneous drain pools. Navigation includes safe-route recall through an authenticated Agent/deck data connection; no Program slot. Outside the special scout link, recall conveys status/arrival messages, not an unlimited sensory or quickhack relay. Stock collision sensors/camera support navigation and ordinary inspection, without the specialist's heightened senses.

**Riding and initiative.** Mount/dismount costs half the rider's movement. While ridden, acts on the rider's initiative as a controlled vehicle: move once, and the board can Dash, Disengage or Dodge. It does not also take an independent scout turn. Normal steering costs no rider Action; a difficult manoeuvre uses the rider's Action and Reflexes (Vehicles), with proficiency if applicable. Rider can otherwise attack or execute a Program normally. When unmounted, a stock board acts on the controller's initiative, moves/Dodges by default; a Bonus Action can command Dash, Disengage, Search or a physically possible object interaction. Commands persist for routine travel outside combat. Mounting or dismounting cannot produce a second board turn in the round. The board provides no cover to a rider. Physically restraining the board stops its travel; rider and board remain distinct attack targets.

**Failure and repairs.** At 0 HP the board disables. A mounted rider uses the standard vehicle failure save: DC 13 Reflexes, 2d6 Bludgeoning on failure, half on success. A separately established high-speed collision replaces this with the actual crash hazard; do not charge both for the same impact. Unloaded flight loses lift on shutdown and suffers ordinary falling damage. At a battery reserve of 2 operating minutes it alerts the controller and attempts a safe landing/stop unless deliberately overridden. HP repair requires actual technical work/parts or an eligible repair Program. Rest does not recharge or repair it.

**Optional Sensor Scout conversion.** Installs a sensor/navigation processor, low-light optical cluster, directional microphones, short-range lidar and chemical sampler, plus a retractable underside service probe/injector. This is a fitted hardware package, not a change into an animal. A Contractor's level 3 Drone Link can bind it as their Sensor Scout. All ordinary Scout restrictions and benefits apply; no second companion. Specialist challenge rating 1/4. Keeps Small size, AC 13, HP 15, payload and propulsion above; abilities become BOD 6 REF 15 CON 13 INT 10 TECH 10 COOL 12. Perception+3, Stealth+4; passive Perception 13; Blindsight 10 feet, Darkvision 60 feet. Advantage on sight/hearing/chemical-sensor Perception and Program saves. The larger hull affects actual openings and concealment, not a blanket Stealth penalty. Fans produce ordinary audible motor noise; use the environment rather than automatic detection.

**Images and relay.** Within 100 feet and a working link, communicates messages and live optical images without Action, Bonus Action or Concentration. ## What a Program Needs



Every Program requires an operational controller (deck or equivalent neural interface), learned/prepared software and its printed execution resources. **Ordinary quickhacking is wireless.** A visible digital target or person with Cyberware is normally reachable within the Program’s printed range. Identifying the target and uploading the effect are included in its execution. Resolve its printed attack or save; there is no preliminary Technology check, discovery action, breach action, cable or pre-established session. A Program with no initial roll does not gain one.

The target’s equipment must provide a plausible cause for the effect. Powered Cyberware can be short-circuited or overheated using its own energy. Neural integration can carry sensory or motor interference through the wearer’s nervous system; a dedicated implant bearing the exact effect’s name is not required. A detached phone does not provide that biological connection. Environmental Programs use suitable nearby systems, materials and energy. Real signal isolation, air gaps or jamming matter only where specifically established, not as default immunity attached to ordinary Cyberware. Secured archives and persistent system administration use ordinary ability checks or deep-dive combat below.
There are no mandatory spoken phrases, gestures or generic V/S/M components. A neural interface executes mentally. A handheld controller requires an available operating hand; physically restrained hands can prevent that input, but do not disable an intact neural controller. Silence does not stop execution. Incapacitation still prevents actions and concentration. No component-removal feature can waive an endpoint, fuel, medical supply, physical barrier or resource payment.

Execution produces a command signature detectable by a monitoring system on the route; physical consequences remain observable. An observer does not automatically know who sent a packet from seeing a victim collapse. Concealment, trace and countermeasures are resolved by the written access rules, not by magic words. Quiet Execution can hide its command signature as explicitly stated in the Neural Adept class.

| Channel | Operative requirement |
|---|---|
| D — Direct quickhack | Reachable compatible electronics or cyberware within a legal target. The addressed hardware must plausibly cause the listed effect: integrated neural Cyberware can carry motor or sensory interference, while powered implants can produce electrical or thermal injury. A passive ornament without powered or neural functionality cannot do either. ICE can be targeted where specified, losing integrity through an explicitly printed Data mode. |
| P — Environmental/physical operation | A reachable electronic actuator plus the necessary real material, energy, mechanism and deployment geometry. Fuel and ignition for a combustion attack; refrigerant for cryogenic effects; a loaded dispenser for chemicals; an actual chassis for drones; actual barriers/tethers for restraint. Organic bystanders can be affected by the resulting real hazard without being hacked. |
| S — Support operation | A willing recipient’s neural interface for predictive motor guidance or biofeedback; real sensors for image processing, or a medical rig and supplies for physical treatment. An ordinary human can receive physical treatment from a real electronically controlled medical device; that does not make their brain directly hackable. |
| I — Information operation | Actual reachable sensors, records, communications or connected analysis hardware. Returns what those sources can establish, with gaps and uncertainty. No narrator secrets, perfect prophecy, mind reading without neural telemetry, or invented records. |
| X — Excluded | No personal program. The source effect has no accepted campaign equivalent and cannot be learned, copied or unlocked through another class feature. |

Each available entry in chapter 06 identifies its requirements and complete numerical operation. The old source name in brackets is identification, not permission to import its fantasy description. A program may have a technological replacement rather than identical target restrictions; the entry says so. All classes use these requirements, including programs paid with Focus, granted by a subclass, executed at will or without a slot.

## Software, devices and Daemons

**Ordinary use is free of Program costs.** Shooting a gun, using monowire, turning on an owned implant, driving your car or operating an authorised camera uses its normal rules. It never consumes an Execution Slot merely because software is involved. A learned Program adds its printed intrusion, automation, prediction, enhancement or attack. It is not the equipment itself. A Cyberdeck and neural interface suffice for neural guidance; an additional implant named after every buff is not required.

**Physical causation.** Direct faults use the victim’s circuits, neural link or motor system. Environmental operations may take over machinery belonging to anyone and coordinate its existing actuators, fuel and payloads. A desk lamp cannot become an industrial laser, and a controller cannot move material without an actuator. Establish the actual opportunity before spending a resource. A Program may improve control, precision or throughput as printed; it does not generate an item. Owned equipment retains its ordinary functions without the Program.

**Security saves.** A device without its own relevant save uses an Intelligence security modifier: consumer +0, commercial +1, secured +2, hardened +4, exceptional +6. Record the grade before resolution, based on its actual security rather than the desired outcome. Roll against the operator’s Program Save DC. Autonomous creatures with an Intelligence save use their own statistic. A driver does not replace a car’s security save. Saves have no automatic natural-1 failure or natural-20 success. Do not use AC to resist a control Program unless that Program expressly calls for an attack roll.

**Environmental takeovers.** A damaging environmental execution uses its printed attack or victim save; there is no additional controller-breach roll. A Program whose purpose is taking sustained control of an unwilling device, chassis or industrial mechanism instead requires one Intelligence security save on acquisition, unless its card already specifies an initial save or contest. This is that takeover’s resolution, not a preliminary check. A successful save prevents control and spends the execution. Willing or already authorised equipment needs no save. Existing source limits on unit numbers, CR, load and commands apply. Controlled units retain their real physical construction; an ordinary service bot cannot acquire a military chassis profile from an upload. Commands cannot grant duplicate actions to a unit already acting under its own controller.

**Daemon** means a persistent software routine. It has only the triggers, targets, duration and actions printed on its card. It supplies no separate consciousness, independent character turn, additional Execution Slots or extra Concentration. A virtual attack origin is a targeting coordinate, not a physical creature or camera; it cannot provide vision, occupancy, cover or Opportunity Attacks. Keep a valid operator/relay route for each new attack. Physical units keep their actual vulnerabilities. Destruction or isolation of a named host ends routines that require it; ordinary uploaded impairments retain their own expiry rules.

**Vehicle control.** Basic locks, lights and horns use ordinary access or Device Pulse. Emergency Brake, Floor It, Vehicle Override, Autopilot Daemon and Turret Override provide distinct combat capabilities in chapter 07. A vehicle moves once per round; seizing its controls never inserts another movement or turn. Maintain its speed, momentum, fuel, load and handling. Existing vehicle rules resolve crashes, cover and passenger harm; neither a takeover nor a failed save is automatic destruction or death. Isolated mechanical controls remain physical. Visible electronic vehicles are otherwise normal wireless targets; military branding alone does not confer immunity.

**Counterplay.** An actual local override, administrator counterhack, Process Termination, isolation or destruction can stop a controlled device as specified. Remote operators expose a return path under the existing tracing rules. Knowing a takeover occurred does not reveal the hacker’s body location. No new intrusion phases, trace currency or compulsory cable is added.

**Medicine and information.** Clinical Programs perform adaptive diagnosis/dosing using treatment cartridges; they are distinct from an airhypo’s fixed emergency effect and do not stack both effects from one dose. Communications and public searches remain ordinary actions. An information Program provides only its stated analysis, decryption, sensor access or exceptional communication; do not charge a slot merely for phoning an expert or reading a public database.

## Construct deployment, acquisition and recall — revision0281

Owned or authorised autonomous hardware accepts its ordinary commands without a Program, Execution Slot or Concentration. Use its equipment card's command timing. A combat mech with an installed targeting controller can receive an attack order; ownership alone does not install navigation, weapons or missing automation. The eight deployment cards in construct-programs.json own their revised operations and are incorporated into the generated catalogue. No ongoing deployment Concentration is required. Concentration during an extended installation, or while holding a readied Program, still follows the ordinary execution rules.

**Acquire an existing chassis.** Respect the Program's range, actual profile, CR, count and size limits. A powered-down unit with live standby electronics and a wake receiver is reachable; an empty battery, isolated controller or disconnected receiver needs an actual power/connection solution. Unsecured or authorised controllers require no security save. A locked standby or hostile active unit makes one Intelligence security save against Program Save DC, using its own relevant save or the device grades above. Each target resolves separately. This is the takeover resolution, not a preliminary check. Successful resistance spends the execution but prevents control of that unit. No AC contest or automatic administrator access is added. Ordinary technical credential work remains an alternative outside instantaneous Program execution.

**Physical continuity.** Record the actual chassis and capabilities before acquisition. Uploads do not refresh HP, fuel, batteries or ammunition, replace a damaged motor, transform a civilian robot into a military chassis, or create a body. Every unit has one turn per round. Keep an existing unit's initiative until the next round when moving it to a deployment group's initiative, so a takeover cannot grant another turn. A new command changes its orders, not its remaining actions. Temporary daemon control does not establish permanent ownership.

### Return tracing and counterattacks

1. **Reach the traffic.** The tracer needs access to the affected network or relay traffic and an active connection to investigate. Observing an injury alone does not supply that access or identify its source.
2. **Trace — Action.** Roll Intelligence (Technology), contested by the connected operator's Intelligence (Technology). Apply normal proficiency and check modifiers. The defending roll costs no Reaction. A tie leaves the operator untraced. This technical action spends no Execution Slot and neither uses armour AC nor Program Save DC as network security.

The path persists while that compromised connection remains usable; another trace is not required for each subsequent attack.
4. **Execute a counterattack.** Eligible electronically delivered Programs can target the identified connected interface through that path without seeing the operator's body. The existing reverse uplink supplies reach to that interface, rather than measuring the operator's physical distance from the camera again. Actual interface isolation can. Neural effects require a biological neural connection; ordinary target immunities, protections and other requirements remain. Physical projectiles, injected substances and environmental explosions cannot travel through the connection.
5. **Break the route.** An operator can spend an Action severing the compromised session, losing their own access through it and preventing new attacks using that route. Destroying or powering down a relay, revoking access or effective jamming can also break the route when the actor can actually do so. Existing uploaded effects follow their own duration and Concentration rules; copied logs and evidence remain. Other independently established routes are unaffected.

These rules work in both directions. A defender can attack or disable the relay instead of tracing its operator. ## Actions, slots and concentration

Program attack = PB + class ability; save DC = 8 + PB + class ability. INT for Netrunner and the two programming subclasses; COOL for other classes. Ordinary Technology intrusion uses INT, independently of program attack/save ability. Utilities cost no slots; tiered programs cost one slot of at least their tier, improving only their printed scaling. A free execution still obeys all requirements and frequency limits. Medical supplies, fuel and ammunition are real inventory; resting restores capacity, not stock.

Only one concentration program may be maintained unless an explicit item says otherwise. Damage requires a CON save, DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher. Separate damage events cause separate saves. Incapacitation or death ends Concentration. A severe environmental disturbance can require a DC 10 Constitution saving throw to maintain it, when the narrator establishes that disturbance. Starting another concentration program ends the first; voluntary ending needs no action. Maintaining requires no action unless the program says it does. An uploaded ongoing effect lasts for its printed duration and concentration. Leaving initial range or disabling wireless reception does not automatically cleanse an already uploaded effect. An operation explicitly requiring continuous remote control needs that connection; turning off its actual actuator can stop a physical output, with the real loss of function that entails. Instantaneous damage and finished fabrication are not reversed by unplugging.

If you execute any Bonus Action Program on your turn, every other Program executed on that same turn must be a Utility with an execution time of one Action. Longer-than-action execution requires spending the action each turn and concentration throughout; interruption wastes time but no slot. Slow mode adds ten minutes and needs explicit class permission. Only a Program with an execution time of one Action can be readied. A readied program spends its slot when readied, requires concentration while held, and uses a reaction on its trigger before the next turn; otherwise it expires. ## Damage types — adopted revision0051

Damage follows the actual mechanism. The ten bodily types are **bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, thermal, cryogenic, electrical, corrosive, toxic, concussive and neural**. Blunt contact/falls are bludgeoning; penetration is piercing; cutting is slashing; heat is thermal; freezing is cryogenic; current is electrical; material corrosion is corrosive; biological poisons are toxic; pressure/sonic waves are concussive; harmful nervous-system stimulation is neural. Original spell names in brackets identify ancestry, not damage categories.

**Data** damage reduces a software instance’s **integrity**. Data does not directly reduce bodily HP. Only an explicit software mode or basic intrusion attack can inflict it; being a direct quickhack alone is insufficient. Physical mode targets a human, chassis or object and uses HP. Neural mode needs a living nervous system and an actual delivery route. Software mode targets the actual instance and uses its virtual AC/ability saves, with normal initiative and action costs. Choose the mode before resolution; one target/event does not damage its software, server and operator together. A physical fire cannot burn ICE. Destroying hardware may end its hosted session as a physical consequence, without a second fictional damage roll.

Default software instances have no elemental resistance, vulnerability or immunity to import from physical profiles. Record actual Data protection before the encounter. The basic watchdog, hardened and military ICE have no Data resistance. A body’s electrical or neural protection does not protect a remote process. All-damage bodily protection applies to the ten bodily types, not to separately hosted software; Data protection must be explicit.

Use the 2014 arithmetic: resistance halves, vulnerability doubles, immunity negates, round down; apply reductions before type protection. Duplicate resistance does not stack. Aggregate same-type components of one damage event before protection; retain distinct types separately. One simultaneous mixed-damage attack is one concentration event. An effect’s printed riders govern conditions, healing prevention and maximum-HP reduction; type alone adds none. Existing HP narration, drop-to-0 injuries and medical recovery remain unchanged.

For **Vulnerability Tag [Hex]** and the damage-rider mode of Persistent Malware [Bestow Curse], add the bonus die in the triggering damage’s primary type. Primary means its direct base damage before enhancement/rider dice. For a genuinely mixed base attack, use its first printed component; explicitly ordered exceptions must be recorded on the card before the encounter. Do not choose after seeing resistance or the roll. A Data attack adds Data. The bonus remains part of the same damage event and follows its protection and critical-hit rules. Nondamaging operations gain no bonus damage.

Target eligibility comes before protection. Toxic does not poison nonliving machines; Corrosive can attack their actual exposed material. Neural cannot injure inert hardware or autonomous software. A biological person with extensive chrome remains a living neural target when reachable. A Data attack cannot injure an offline person. Ordinary armour supplies its stated AC, not automatic damage resistance; a type does not bypass AC or add a new defence statistic. Electrical damage does not automatically stun or double against robots. Thermal does not automatically ignite a person. Payloads and eligible interfaces remain actual requirements.

Examples: Short Circuit physical mode rolls 1d10 Electrical per hit; software mode rolls 1d10 Data per hit. With Vulnerability Tag active, the physical hit is 1d10+1d6 Electrical; the software hit is 1d10+1d6 Data. A rifle hit adds Piercing for its Tag rider. Electrical resistance halves the complete Electrical event, not its attack roll. Neural Spike’s Neural mode cannot damage a robot, but its separate Data mode can attack a reachable software instance. The adopted overhaul replaces the earlier fantasy-category mapping. Protection features and program entries specify their new mechanisms directly. ### Critical Injuries

**Trigger:** the first time damaging harm reduces a living target from positive HP to 0 HP in an encounter, record one critical injury appropriate to the harm. Critical hits alone do not trigger an injury; their extra damage makes reaching 0 more likely. Damage from attacks, saving-throw effects and hazards can all trigger this rule. Apply it equally to player and NPC combatants who survive. Repeated drops during the same encounter do not generate additional injury rolls; damage and failed death saves still apply normally. A feature that leaves the target at 1 HP prevents this trigger. An emergency injector that restores HP after damage reaches 0 does not erase the injury. A deliberate nonlethal knockout or an effect that causes unconsciousness without damaging harm does not automatically create a lasting injury.

For physical harm, roll the existing recorded d6 injury table: 1 leg (speed −10 feet); 2 arm (disadvantage on checks using that arm, not all attacks); 3 concussion (disadvantage Investigation and Perception); 4 torso (maximum HP reduced by PB); 5 sensory trauma (disadvantage on one specified sight/hearing-based check type); 6 bleeding (cannot spend Hit Dice until treated). If the mechanism or a previously established hit location makes entries impossible, establish the eligible entries before the injury roll and select uniformly among them. Neural feedback cannot invent a broken leg. Record the actual injury, treatment and recovery clock. Identical penalties do not stack; a new critical injury to the same site renews that site's treatment requirement and recovery clock. Different critical injuries from separate encounters or explicit hazards can coexist.

**Short Rest:** one hour of light activity. Recover the normal short-rest class resources, including Contractor Execution Slots. No automatic HP and no spending Hit Dice merely for resting.

**Long rest:** retain the 2014 eight-hour requirements, interruption rule, once-per-24-hours limit and requirement to start with at least 1 HP. Recover normal class resources and half total Hit Dice, minimum one. With adequate food and water, regain **HP equal to your Constitution modifier, minimum 1**, up to your current HP maximum. This natural recovery is available once per 24 hours through the qualifying Long Rest; it spends no Hit Die or medical supply. It is additional to medical convalescence when that treatment also qualifies. HP recovery does not remove critical injuries or their penalties, and any explicit effect preventing HP recovery still applies. Recovered Hit Dice can be spent only through the convalescence procedure; the same eight hours may satisfy both procedures when all their requirements are met. Exhaustion recovery remains below.

**Convalescence:** once per 24 hours, after eight hours of rest with food, water and appropriate first aid; any critical injuries must have been treated, spend up to one quarter of total Hit Dice, rounded up. Each restores its roll + CON modifier, minimum zero. A stocked clinic with a qualified attendant increases this allowance to half total Hit Dice, rounded up. This is the only routine opportunity to spend Hit Dice. At least one die is allowed. Medical treatment supplies are consumed; sleeping in an alley with an untreated gunshot does not qualify. If no injury exists, ordinary first aid is sufficient. Recovery Coaching adds its die once to this recovery, rather than to a Short Rest. Durable applies normally. At level 8, home convalescence permits two dice a day; a clinic permits four. These are authored game rates, not medical predictions.

**Airhypo:** a reusable injector delivers one purchased recovery dose as an action to self or a willing/unconscious recipient in reach. Standard dose restores 2d4+2 HP; enhanced 4d4+4; surgical 8d4+8; intensive 10d4+20. All grades share **one effective dose per recipient per 24 hours**, measured from administration, not from sleeping. Additional doses consume supplies without restoring HP. An airhypo cannot remove an injury, cure infection, reset death, refill class resources or regenerate tissue. The emergency injector implant consumes the same dose and uses the same recipient clock. An injector is equipment; doses are consumables.

**Medical programs and class recovery:** retain their printed HP amounts, actions and class-resource costs. A cartridge is a standard medical consumable, not a costly spell component, and a focus cannot replace it. Sustained programs consume one cartridge per recipient when first treated, not per tick. Each cartridge supports only that activation; Short Rests do not manufacture replacements. Record the inventory and obtain a dated medical quote before purchase. No critical injury disappears from repeated low-tier programs. Clinical Efficiency and similar bonuses add HP to the same administration without consuming another cartridge.

Second Wind and other innate self-recovery remain their printed limited-use HP recovery: they represent rallying and pain control, never closing a wound. Continuous innate recovery such as Survivor also leaves injuries and their penalties intact. Medical-reserve features consume a cartridge per recipient per activation when restoring HP. Temporary HP is protective margin, never wound repair, and never revives at 0. Stabilisation requires kit supplies or a functioning stabiliser but no treatment cartridge unless it also restores HP. Ration-derived HP restoration consumes the prepared ration and follows its printed limits; it cannot treat an injury. These distinctions are explicit exceptions, not a discretionary surcharge added during combat.

### Treating an injury

A critical injury from the above table needs one hour of first aid and a stocked kit: routine treatment by a qualified clinician succeeds; pressured/improvised treatment uses Medicine DC 15. Failure consumes the time and supplies but permits a new attempt with better conditions or another clinician. Treatment stops the bleeding entry's restriction immediately; other penalties persist until recovery. Full HP does not suppress them.

A standard critical injury heals after **seven completed convalescence days** following successful treatment. A day qualifies with eight hours' rest and no combat, strenuous labour or further HP damage. A nonqualifying day adds no progress but does not erase prior days. A major critical injury—one complicated by a failed death save during the associated incapacitation—takes **21 qualifying days** and needs surgical treatment before progress begins. No random amputation is added by this rule. Multiple injuries heal concurrently; record each clock. Untreated injuries make no progress.

Surgery requires an appropriate clinic, clinician, four hours and medical supplies. Successful surgery halves remaining recovery days, rounded up, once per injury; it does not remove the penalty instantly. Routine surgery succeeds under proper conditions; pressured surgery uses Medicine DC 20. Failure adds one recovery day and requires stabilisation, not an invented instant death. The converted Heal program can perform first aid for one injury alongside restoring HP; it cannot replace surgery or recovery days. Reconstructive Treatment (Regenerate) supplies its initial clinical treatment in one hour; structural reconstruction still requires seven qualifying days.

**Prosthetic replacement:** replacing the affected limb or organ can remove that injury after the implant's installation and postoperative recovery. Use the longer of three days or the implant's specified recovery period; ordinary replacement has Load 0, enhancements retain their Load. Surgery does not cure an unrelated concussion, infection or torso injury. Replacement cannot be performed by inserting a chip or using an airhypo. Prices and availability depend on the clinic and equipment.

Example: after a hit drops the operator to 0 and the injury roll identifies the leg, an airhypo can restore 7 HP while leaving the critical leg injury with speed reduced by 10 feet. A qualifying fed and hydrated Long Rest restores his Execution Slots and max(1, Constitution modifier) HP, while the leg injury and its penalty persist. Clinical care helps recover HP; the leg's treatment clock or a replacement procedure resolves its penalty.

Retain 2014 exhaustion: level 1 disadvantage ability checks; 2 speed halved; 3 disadvantage attacks and saves; 4 HP maximum halved; 5 speed 0; 6 death. Effects accumulate. A fed, hydrated Long Rest removes one level. Do not use revised −2-per-level exhaustion. Rest is possible in a secure ordinary room; a luxury hotel is not a mechanical prerequisite.

**Level and resources.** A feature's level means level in that class. PB means proficiency bonus, determined by total character level. SR means a short rest of at least one hour of light activity; LR means a long rest of at least eight hours, including at least six hours of sleep and no more than two hours of light activity, available once per 24 hours. At least one hour of strenuous activity interrupts an LR and requires restarting it. You must have at least 1 HP at its start to benefit. A Short Rest restores no HP automatically. A qualifying Long Rest with adequate food and water restores HP equal to the Constitution modifier, minimum 1, once per 24 hours and up to the current HP maximum; injury-specific recovery restrictions still apply. Medical convalescence, injuries and Hit Dice follow chapter 01. A class resource returns only at its specified rest; ammunition, fuel, medical supplies and destroyed equipment do not.

**Hit points.** At character level 1 take the maximum class Hit Die plus CON modifier. Each subsequent level, including a first level in a new class, adds the fixed die average (d6:4; d8:5; d10:6; d12:7) plus CON modifier, minimum 1. Gain one Hit Die of the class's size. A CON modifier change adjusts maximum HP by the difference times total character level. Only the first class grants its saving throw proficiencies and full starting skill/equipment package; chapter 05 gives multiclass entry benefits.

**Ability improvement (ASI).** At each marked level, increase one score by 2 or two different scores by 1, maximum 20, or select an eligible chapter 05 feat. The improvement happens once, not once per table column. A subclass feature never replaces an ASI unless expressly stated. Repeated features of the same name do not stack.

**Extra Attack.** Two weapon attacks instead of one when taking the Attack action on your turn. Solo eventually gains three/four. It never multiplies a program, grenade, readied attack or reaction. Extra Attack from different classes does not stack. An attack may be replaced by a grapple or shove under chapter 01.

**Program execution.** Utilities are tier 0 and consume no slot. Tiered programs spend one available slot of at least their tier; higher slots improve only the scaling explicitly printed on the program. Full/half-caster slots return on LR; Contractor slots return on SR/LR. Program attack = PB + class execution modifier; program save DC = 8 + PB + that modifier. Netrunner and the two one-third-caster subclasses use INT; all other program classes use COOL. Knowing software never supplies its target hardware, fuel or medical supplies. Chapter 02 and each program's requirements always apply, including to at-will, subclass and no-slot executions.

**Learned programs.** A known-program class selects entries from its own list at tiers its own single-class table can execute. On gaining a level in that class it can replace one known tiered program with another eligible entry. Utilities cannot be routinely swapped. Bonus subclass lists add choices only unless expressly described as always prepared or granted. No program is automatically learned because it appears in a catalogue or expanded list.

**Prepared programs.** Choose the stated number after an LR, minimum one, from the class list or personal library specified below. Preparing takes one minute per tier of each selected program. Prepared entries remain until changed; executing one does not unprepare it. Always-prepared subclass programs are additional to that count, use the class's execution ability, and count as that class's programs even if normally absent from its list. Preparation and copying use the class's own level, never higher multiclass slots.

**Slow mode.** If a class permits it, an entry tagged ritual can execute with ten additional minutes and no slot, at its minimum tier. Longer execution requires concentration throughout; interruption wastes the time but not a slot. Supplies and endpoint access still apply. Slow mode is unavailable without an explicit class/feat permission.

**Equipment and class hardware.** Starting kits are defined in chapter 00; a special penniless opening overrides possessions. The class gives training and software; bought/issued hardware must actually be carried or installed. A specific feature granting a drone or suit gives only the item and functions it names, never a module for every program. Physical replacement or fitting requires a safe workbench and one hour, plus actual replacement parts. An earned feature is not delayed for extra XP or training, but missing equipment cannot function. Cyberware Load belongs to purchased enhancements, not a second charge for an already granted class feature. Program restrictions do not stop ordinary non-program speech, skill use, weapon attacks or physical class features.
